prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured driver reported a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact will go through the attorney's office from here.

Entry 2: The insured driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force for the period at issue. Nothing so far suggests the reported damage existed before coverage began.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck and back strain. The kind and force of the impact described fit that injury well. No earlier injury to the same areas is known from the records we have.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage was inspected and is consistent with the impact as described. A few older scratches are present, and they may predate this collision, so they have been noted separately for the estimate.

Entry 5: Police records place the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witness to the collision itself has come forward, and no photographs or separate accident report have been provided by anyone.

Entry 6: In the first call, the claimant described the direction of impact and the number of occupants in the car. In a later conversation those details were different, and the claimant has not yet explained the change. Counsel has been asked to clarify in writing.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of injury. The treating provider's notes are requested to confirm the reasons for the extended course of care.

Entry 8: File remains open pending the requested treatment notes, the written clarification on the impact details, and a review of the scratches against the inspection photos. No liability or coverage decision has been made.
